title: Who pays for urban environment management? The role of the third-party service provider
summary: The dominant contemporary paradigm of direct state-led urban environmental regulation entails significant risks, including high administrative burden, frequent conflicts with polluting entities, and economic vulnerabilities for those sources. To address these deficiencies, this paper integrates third-party service provider (TPSP) into China's existing management framework as a beneficial extension beyond conventional government intervention.
